subject: Cross-functional weekly sync — QBR asks & exception manifest
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@aurelia.com>
Cc: procurement@aurelia.com
Date: Tue, 28 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-functional weekly sync — QBR asks & exception manifest

Thanks all for a tight sync this morning. Pulling the notes and next steps into a single manifest so execs have a clean view for QBR prep. High-level: Aurelia's trial expanded unexpectedly on private deployment, a handful of model-regression flags popped in our QA, and they expect a firm rollout ETA for next-month feature gates.

Please see the initial asks and owners below (also attached: QBR-exception-manifest.xlsx):

- Product: confirm whether the v2 batching change can be gated behind a config flag by 04/06. (owner: karthik)
- Infra/Runtime: provide tokenized latency numbers for sequences >2048 tokens for dedicated pool. (owner: vivek; deliverable: latency.csv)
- Customer Ops: finalize mutual action plan and procurement pre-reqs for private deploy. (owner: kimberly; attachment: mutual-action-plan-Aurelia.pdf)
- Exec ask: bundle an executive note (1-pager) summarizing risks, mitigations, and go/no-go recommendation by 04/03. (owner: marissa)

Quick asks in prioritization order: gating flag, latency numbers, mutual action plan, exec 1-pager. If anything slips, flag here and I will escalate to GTM leadership.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: QBR-exception-manifest.xlsx (spreadsheet summary)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@aurelia.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-functional weekly sync — QBR asks & exception manifest

Thanks Marissa — noted. Quick notes from Product: we can add a runtime gating flag for the batching change, but it will require a short code path for model selection and config evaluation; estimate 5 dev days including QA. Targeting PR by 04/04 if we start tomorrow.

Requests for infra/data to make the recommendation airtight:
- Vivek: need current p95/p99 for 1k and 2k token windows for dedicated pool (baseline + with kv-cache priming)
- QA: list of failing prompts that triggered the regression (small sample) — if you can paste 10 flagged prompts that will help.

I will start a short doc with the trade-offs and keep it to 1 page for the exec ask.

-- Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Serving
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@aurelia.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-functional weekly sync — QBR asks & exception manifest

On Wed, 29 Mar 2028 at 10:03, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — noted. Quick notes from Product: we can add a runtime gating flag for the batching change...

Attaching the baseline latency snapshot we pulled from the dedicated pool telemetry. Summary here (full CSV on the Drive link):
- p95 (1k tokens): 120ms
- p99 (1k tokens): 210ms
- p95 (2k tokens): 190ms
- p99 (2k tokens): 360ms

We also captured a KV-cache priming run — latencies drop ~18% p95 for repeated prefixes. Will upload latency.csv to the shared folder this afternoon. If Product wants a staged rollout, infra can provision a blue pool and route 10% traffic for a week.

-Vivek
Senior Infra Engineer, Runtime
Attachments: latency.csv (telemetry snapshot)
From: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@aurelia.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, procurement@aurelia.com, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Mar 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-functional weekly sync — QBR asks & exception manifest

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying items from our side: 

1) Procurement: we need a templated SOC2/legals checklist and expected timeline for onboarding a private deploy (our procurement team is copied). Can Kimberly confirm if any additional evidence is required beyond the standard pack?

2) Rollout: the blue pool sounds sensible. Can you also include an estimate for cost delta for a 10% blue pool for 1 month? Our finance lead wants a ballpark.

If you can capture those two items in the mutual action plan by next Wednesday (04/06), we should be aligned for QBR review.

Best,
Anna Lopez
Head of Product Operations, Aurelia Systems
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@aurelia.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2028 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cross-functional weekly sync — QBR asks & exception manifest

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Anna. Quick commitments and owners (finalizing by 04/06):

- Kimberly: confirm SOC2 artifact list + any additional evidence for private deploy; produce mutual-action-plan-Aurelia.pdf by 04/06.
- Vivek: upload latency.csv and provide a 10% blue-pool cost delta estimate (ballpark) by 04/05.
- Karthik: PR for gating flag by 04/04 and the 1-page exec note draft by 04/03.
- Marissa: will compile the exec 1-pager and circulate to GTM leads for signoff on 04/03 afternoon.

If anyone anticipates slippage, reply-all and flag — I will raise to GTM if we miss targets. Otherwise I will circulate the final manifest + 1-pager on 04/03 evening ahead of QBR dry-run.

Thanks team,
Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
